races.title: State House, District 67
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Cody Huneycutt
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 67 (Stanly and Montgomery counties) since January 2025. Cattle farmer. Worked about eight years as a staff member in the N.C. House before taking office. Holds degrees from Stanly Community College and UNC Charlotte.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Huneycutt on data centers. We found no record of his position on homestead property taxes specifically, on limits for institutional or foreign land buyers, on H-1B or immigration enforcement, on police pay, on abortion, or on school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site says only that he supports cutting taxes in general and wants more parental voice in schools. His sponsored-bill list was not readable on the pages we had, so apart from the Wikipedia mention of H.B. 859 we could not review his sponsored legislation. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. His birth and upbringing in Stanly County come only from his own campaign website, and we found no independent confirmation. The staff-career details are also mainly from his campaign site, with Wikipedia saying he worked for Wayne Sasser.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Stanly County, still lives there and tends a cattle farm there; Wikipedia also says he lives in Stanly County.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has held the N.C. House District 67 seat since January 2025. Before that he spent about eight years as a House staff member, advising on policy in the Finance, Unemployment Insurance, Banking and Revenue Laws, Health and Appropriations committees. He also runs a cattle farm.
qual.why: He has legislative service as a sitting member (one term) plus a long career in legislative policy and budget staff work, which fits the high band. The score is held below the top because he has served only one term and the staff-work details come mainly from his own campaign site.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site pledges to fight for farmland preservation and to keep rural farmland available for future generations, and says affordable groceries cannot be expected when housing developments are planted where crops have always been.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Stanly County, still lives there and tends a cattle farm there; Wikipedia also says he lives in Stanly County.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site: "We cannot expect affordable groceries when housing developments are being planted where crops have always been," and he promises to fight to keep rural farmland available for generations.

cands.name: Jocelyn Torres
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 67 in 2026. Born and raised in Stanly County, she graduated from UNC Greensboro in 2023 and says she has worked for the Stanly County school system. She has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended in the voter guide 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We found no details on her work history, including her role and dates with the Stanly County school system. We found no news coverage, interviews or public statements from her on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth and development, immigration, policing, guns, or abortion. We found no documented controversies. Her birthplace and upbringing come only from her own campaign materials and Ballotpedia survey, and we found no independent record to confirm them.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign website and her Ballotpedia survey both say she was born and raised in Stanly County, and she graduated from Albemarle High School there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: UNC Greensboro graduate (2023, Political Science and Psychology), Model UN participant, and volunteer English teacher for nonprofits. She says she worked for the Stanly County school system, but the role and dates are not given. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: She is a first-time candidate with no legislative, policy, budget or business record that can be confirmed, so she falls in the low range. The school-system job is acknowledged, but its role and length are unknown.
qual.label: She is a first-time candidate with no legislative, policy, budget or business record that can be confirmed, so she falls in the low range. The school-system job is acknowledged, but its role and length are unknown.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said in her Ballotpedia survey that students and educators deserve competitive pay and that she will support legislation that fully funds public schools. She did not address vouchers, charters or school choice.
